transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2028-01-09
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes (recording started at 15:02)
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Jenna (Skyhaven Head ML), Marcus (VP Eng), Sara (CTO), Owen (SRE)

Summary:
Redwood AE/SE walked through host/dedicated/private tradeoffs focused on per-token unit economics, batching and KV caching levers, and tenancy/residency constraints for Skyhaven's conversational and recommendation traffic. Customer is cost constrained, targets 99th pct latency < 350ms for interactive flows, and has an upcoming pilot in 6 weeks. Discussed SOC2/KMS/VPC concerns and proposed next steps for workload traces and a benchmarking session.

Topics:
- Per-token pricing and how it maps to their prompt sizes and completions
- Batching and caching levers (prefix caching, KV cache warm strategies)
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (security and latency tradeoffs)
- Tenanting: multi-tenant noisy neighbor concerns and rate limiting
- Pilot scope and timelines

Questions (raised during call):
- "How much will batching help our p99 for short completions?"
- "Can KV cache be shared across tenants or must it be per-customer?"
- "What are the pricing deltas for peak burst vs reserved throughput?"

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do intros quickly, then Liam will dig into the econ levers. Jenna, do you want to kick with your quick context?
[00:12] Jenna (Skyhaven - Head of ML): Sure, thanks. So high level, um, Skyhaven runs conversational checkout assistants and in-app recommendations. Latency matters for conversion, cost matters for margins. We're trying to see — hosted vs dedicated vs private — what's the best mix. Pilot in about 6 weeks, want to keep costs under a threshold.
[00:27] Marcus (VP Eng): To add, our traffic is spiky; mornings peak and weekends are lighter. We have multi-tenant stores on the same cluster today and are worried about noisy neighbor.
[00:35] Liam (Redwood SE): Got it. We'll try to map per-token pricing to your workload and show batching/cache levers. Quick question — average prompt + completion length?
[00:42] Jenna: For chat agents it's about 80 tokens input and 60 tokens output average, but 5-10% long tails up to 600 tokens for receipts and order histories. Recommendation calls are smaller ~30 in, 8 out.
[00:55] Owen (SRE): Also our SLO is p99 under 350ms for the chat path. We can tolerate some tail to 500ms but conversion drops after 400.
[01:04] Maya: Thanks. Okay Liam, walk us through the unit econ model please.
[01:09] Liam: Sure. So simple mapping — hosted pricing is per-token served with tiered volume discounts. For dedicated we model reserved GPU capacity which reduces per-token cost for sustained throughput because we amortize instance cost. The levers you have are: batching, which increases GPU utilization lowering cost per token but increases queuing introduce latency; prefix or KV caching, which avoids re-computing token sequences and can reduce compute by 30-70% depending on reuse, and quantization or smaller model variants for non-critical flows.
[01:35] Jenna: Quick question — for KV cache you mean the key-value of past attention? Will it be shared between stores?
[01:41] Liam: Good point. We recommend a per-tenant KV cache to avoid cross-tenant leakage; technically you can share cache if all tenants are same trust domain, but that raises data residency and security concerns. Also our runtime supports prefix caching: standard prefix reuse for system prompts and common histories.
[01:57] Sara (CTO): On privacy we need SOC2, KMS integration for keys, and audit logging with 1 year retention. Private deployment may be needed if we can't allow shared caches.
[02:07] Maya: Understood. For SOC2 + KMS we can offer Redwood Private with a customer-managed KMS, or Dedicated in a customer VPC with KMS. Both options support audit logs, but Private gives you full control and on-prem option.
[02:20] Marcus: Cost-wise what's the ballpark difference between hosted and reserved dedicated?
[02:25] Liam: It depends on utilization. Example: for sustained 100 RPS with average tokens per request 140, hosted per-token ends up around $0.0008 per token in our hypothetical tier, dedicated reserved could push per-token to $0.0003 if utilization is high and you get autoscaling granularity. But if your utilization swings and you have to overprovision, dedicated costs go up. We usually present a blended model: hosted for burst and Dedicated for base load.
[02:49] Jenna: That gap seems big. How do batching numbers change p99?
[02:53] Liam: Batching increases throughput; if you batch aggressively you might increase p99 by 40-60ms depending on queue window. For short completions, small micro-batching (e.g., 2-8 requests) increases GPU efficiency with minimal latency impact. Larger batch windows (50-200ms) help throughput but hurt tail. We can tune real traffic in the benchmarking.
[03:15] Owen: Are there automatic burst policies? We need to handle holiday spikes.
[03:18] Maya: Yes, Dedicated supports burst capacity pools and Redwood will auto-fallback to hosted if Dedicated is saturated — that gives you both capacity and resiliency. We can define policies per route.
[03:28] Marcus: What about model variants — can we route low-risk flows to smaller models?
[03:31] Liam: Absolutely. Smart routing can send certain endpoints to quantized models or smaller families. That's one of the larger knobs for cost reduction without changing UX too much.
[03:40] Jenna: For KV cache warm-up, what are realistic hit rates?
[03:43] Liam: For conversational assistants with reusable system prompts and similar user intents, 40-60% for prefix caching is common. KV cache for long contexts is trickier — with good partitioning and TTLs you can hit 20-30% of tokens avoided on average, though some customers see up to 70% on tightly repeated patterns.
[03:58] Sara: If we do per-tenant caches, does that mean more memory cost on cohorts?
[04:02] Liam: Yes memory and capacity planning differ. Per-tenant caches increase total memory but avoid cross-tenant data mixing. We typically size KV cache per tenant by active session count plus average context length.
[04:12] Owen: Any thought on routing by latency vs cost? We want p99 strict for checkout flows but ok to save cost on recommendations.
[04:18] Maya: You can set route policies: strict SLO route pinned to low-latency hardware and kept on Dedicated; non-critical routes go to hosted or smaller models. That gives predictable p99 for checkout.
[04:28] Marcus: How granular is billing? Per-token per-route?
[04:31] Liam: Hosted is per-token per model variant. For Dedicated we break down token-equivalent cost in the billing sheet — we show effective per-token cost after reserving capacity and including infra. We also pass through GPU utilization metrics so you can map.
[04:44] Jenna: What's typical timeline for Private?
[04:46] Maya: Private on VPC with Redwood-managed control plane takes 4-6 weeks; full on-prem bundles can take longer depending on your ops. Dedicated can be provisioned faster, days to a week, depending on region.
[04:56] Owen: For the pilot can we get a short dedicated cluster?
[04:59] Liam: Yes we can provision a pilot dedicated pool for benchmark week; we'll need load traces and expected concurrency to size it.
[05:06] Sara: Security — SSO/SAML, RBAC, and audit trails are musts. Also data residency in EU for some customers.
[05:13] Maya: All supported. We'll include compliance docs and our data residency patterns.
[05:18] Marcus: One more — how do you handle model rollouts and potential regressions?
[05:22] Liam: Redwood Console has rollout controls (canary, % rollouts), model-level quality monitoring, and eval hooks to compare outputs on a prompt set. If quality drops, automatic fallback to previous model or variant is possible.
[05:36] Jenna: Good. For numbers, can you give a worked example for our 100 RPS baseline?
[05:40] Liam: We'll do that offline with your traces — but quick math: 100 RPS * 140 tokens = 14k tokens per second -> about 1.2 billion tokens/day. Multiply by per-token hosted price gives daily spend; with batching and caching we can often reduce compute by 30-50% effective. We'll put a worked spreadsheet in the pricing doc.
[06:02] Maya: Great, let's wrap with next steps. We'll share the price sheet, you share traces, and we'll schedule the benchmark. Any final questions?
[06:12] Marcus: No, just confirm the date window for benchmarking week of Jan 22.
[06:16] Maya: We'll propose three slots after we get traces. Thanks everyone.

Recap & next steps (verbal):
- Redwood to send hosted vs dedicated vs private pricing spreadsheet and a sample unit econ model.
- Skyhaven to upload 7-day request traces and sample prompts.
- Schedule benchmarking session (2-hour) week of Jan 22 with dedicated pilot cluster.

End of meeting.
